title: Credit score (CIBIL) — what it is and how to build it
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: A credit score is a 3-digit number, 300 to 900, that summarises how reliably you repay borrowed money. In India, bureaus such as CIBIL, Experian, Equifax and CRIF High Mark calculate it; a score of 750 or above is generally considered good and helps you get loans and cards at lower interest. What moves it: paying every EMI and card bill on time (the biggest factor), keeping credit-card usage below about 30% of your limit, a long credit history, a healthy mix of credit, and not applying for many loans at once (each application triggers a 'hard enquiry'). Checking your own score is a 'soft enquiry' and does not hurt it; by RBI rule you can get one free full credit report per year from each bureau. If you have no history, a small credit card paid in full every month is the usual way to start. Beware of anyone who promises to 'fix' your score for a fee.
summary_hinglish: Credit score 300-900 ka number hai jo batata hai tum loan kitni bharosemand tarah se chukate ho. 750+ achha maana jaata hai. EMI aur card bill time par bharo, card limit ka 30% se kam use karo, bahut saare loans ek saath apply mat karo. Apna score check karne se score nahi girta.
summary_hi: क्रेडिट स्कोर 300 से 900 के बीच का नंबर है जो बताता है कि आप कर्ज़ कितनी भरोसेमंदी से चुकाते हैं। 750+ अच्छा माना जाता है। EMI और कार्ड बिल समय पर भरें, कार्ड लिमिट का 30% से कम इस्तेमाल करें। अपना स्कोर देखने से वह नहीं गिरता।
